title: Chapter 4 Quiz 5
description: Sorting by swapping neighbours that are out of order.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: What does **bubble sort** do?
options: Repeatedly swaps adjacent elements that are in the wrong order
Picks the smallest element each time
questions.explanation: Neighbouring pairs are compared and swapped when needed.

questions.question: In ascending bubble sort, when are two neighbours swapped?
options: When the left one is greater than the right one
When the left one is smaller
questions.explanation: array[j] > array[j+1] means the pair is in the wrong order.

questions.question: Complete the bubble sort of 5 elements.
questions.code:
For i From 1 To 4 Do
    For j From 1 To {{1}} Do
        If array[j] {{2}} array[j + 1] Then
            temp ← array[j]
            array[j] ← array[j + 1]
            array[j + 1] ← temp
        EndIf
    EndFor
EndFor
questions.explanation: The inner loop stops at 5 - i because the end is already sorted. We swap when the left is greater.

questions.question: Sort [5, 1, 4, 2, 8] with bubble sort. Give the array after each pass.
questions.explanation: Each pass moves the largest remaining value to the right end.

questions.question: After the first pass of bubble sort, where is the largest element?
questions.explanation: The big value bubbles up to the last position.

questions.question: Bubble sort is rarely used in production.
questions.explanation: It is simple and educational, but slow: O(n²).

questions.question: Which is the time complexity of bubble sort in the course?
questions.explanation: Two nested loops over the data give O(n²).
